Entries with an empty 'sanskrit' field are meaning-only; the verse text is to be added.

verses.meaning: Disease is imbalance of the doshas; balance of the doshas is health.

verses.topic: Signs of a healthy person (svastha lakshana)
verses.sanskrit: samadoṣaḥ samāgniśca samadhātumalakriyaḥ / prasannātmendriyamanāḥ svastha ityabhidhīyate
verses.meaning: A healthy person has balanced doshas and agni, normal functioning of dhatus and malas, and a clear, content self, senses and mind.

verses.sanskrit: vāyuḥ pittaṃ kaphaścoktaḥ śārīro doṣasaṃgrahaḥ / mānasaḥ punaruddiṣṭo rajaśca tama eva ca
verses.meaning: Vata, pitta and kapha are the bodily doshas; rajas and tamas are the doshas of the mind.

verses.topic: Nidana Panchaka - five means of diagnosis
verses.sanskrit: nidānaṃ pūrvarūpāṇi rūpāṇyupaśayastathā / samprāptiśceti vijñānaṃ rogāṇāṃ pañcadhā smṛtam
verses.meaning: A disease is understood through five means: cause, prodromal signs, signs and symptoms, upashaya (diagnostic response) and samprapti (pathogenesis).

verses.topic: Mandagni as the root of disease
verses.meaning: All diseases arise when agni is weak, udara roga most of all.

verses.sanskrit: viruddhāhāraceṣṭasya mandāgnerniścalasya ca / snigdhaṃ bhuktavato hyannaṃ vyāyāmaṃ kurvatastathā // vāyunā prerito hyāmaḥ śleṣmasthānaṃ pradhāvati / ...
verses.meaning: Amavata arises in one with incompatible diet and conduct, weak agni and a sedentary life, or who exercises after a heavy, unctuous meal; ama, propelled by vata, moves to the seats of kapha (the joints).

verses.sanskrit: aṅgamardo'ruciścatṛṣṇā hyālasyaṃ gauravaṃ jvaraḥ / apākaḥ śūnatāṅgānāmāmavātasya lakṣaṇam
verses.meaning: Body ache, loss of taste, thirst, lethargy, heaviness, fever, indigestion and swelling of the body parts are the signs of Amavata.
When aggravated, Amavata causes painful swelling of the joints of the hands, feet, head, ankles, sacrum, knees and thighs; the affected part hurts as if stung by scorpions.

verses.sanskrit: laṅghanaṃ svedanaṃ tiktaṃ dīpanāni kaṭūni ca / virecanaṃ snehapānaṃ bastayaścāmamārute
verses.meaning: In Amavata: fasting (langhana), sudation, bitter and pungent agni-kindling drugs, purgation, internal oleation and basti.

verses.sanskrit: āsyāsukhaṃ svapnasukhaṃ dadhīni grāmyaudakānūparasāḥ payāṃsi / navānnapānaṃ guḍavaikṛtaṃ ca pramehahetuḥ kaphakṛcca sarvam
verses.meaning: Causes of prameha: indulgence in sitting and sleep, curd, meat of domestic, aquatic and marshy animals, milk, new grains and drinks, jaggery products, and everything that increases kapha.

verses.sanskrit: sthūlaḥ pramehī balavānihaikaḥ kṛśastathaikaḥ paridurbalaśca / saṃbṛṃhaṇaṃ tatra kṛśasya kāryaṃ saṃśodhanaṃ doṣabalādhikasya
verses.meaning: Prameha patients are of two kinds: obese and strong, or lean and weak. The lean are nourished; the strong with excess dosha receive purification (shodhana).
Overeating, heavy, sweet, cold and unctuous food, lack of exercise, day sleep and lack of mental exertion cause excessive obesity.

verses.topic: Sthaulya - eight defects of the obese
verses.sanskrit: āyuṣo hrāso javoparodhaḥ kṛcchravyavāyatā daurbalyaṃ daurgandhyaṃ svedābādhaḥ kṣudatimātraṃ pipāsātiyogaśceti
verses.meaning: The obese suffer shortened life, reduced agility, difficulty in sexual function, weakness, body odour, excessive sweating, excessive hunger and excessive thirst.

verses.topic: Sthaulya - pathogenesis (meda obstructs vata in the koshtha)
verses.meaning: Meda obstructs the channels; vata, confined to the koshtha, kindles agni and absorbs food quickly, so the obese person craves food and grows fatter.

verses.topic: Sthaulya and karshya - principle of treatment
verses.sanskrit: guru cātarpaṇaṃ ceṣṭaṃ sthūlānāṃ karśanaṃ prati / kṛśānāṃ bṛṃhaṇārthaṃ ca laghu santarpaṇaṃ ca yat
verses.meaning: To reduce the obese, give food that is heavy yet non-nourishing; to build up the emaciated, food that is light yet nourishing.

verses.sanskrit: vātaghnānyannapānāni śleṣmamedoharāṇi ca / rūkṣoṣṇā bastayastīkṣṇā rūkṣāṇyudvartanāni ca
verses.meaning: For the obese: food and drink that pacify vata and reduce kapha and meda, dry and hot sharp enemas, and dry powder massage (udvartana).
In pregnancy, strong purification (vamana, virechana), harsh and sharp drugs, heavy exertion and fasting are to be avoided because they harm the foetus.

verses.sanskrit: viruddhaduṣṭāmlavidāhipittaprakopipānānnabhujo vidagdham / pittaṃ svahetūpacitaṃ purā yat tadamlapittaṃ pravadanti santaḥ
verses.meaning: When pitta, already increased by its own causes, is further vitiated by incompatible, spoiled, sour, burning and pitta-provoking food and drink, it becomes 'vidagdha' and is called Amlapitta.
Indigestion, fatigue, nausea, bitter-sour belching, heaviness, burning in the chest and throat, and loss of taste indicate Amlapitta.

verses.topic: Red flags in dyspepsia - refer before treating
verses.meaning: Black (tarry) stools, vomiting of blood, difficulty swallowing, unintended weight loss, anaemia or new symptoms after 45 years are alarm features. Refer for endoscopy and blood tests before treating as simple Amlapitta.

verses.sanskrit: pratilomaṃ yadā vāyuḥ srotāṃsi pratipadyate / grīvāṃ śiraśca saṅgṛhya śleṣmāṇaṃ samudīrya ca ... āsīno labhate saukhyamuṣṇaṃ caivābhinandati
verses.meaning: Vata moving in the reverse direction enters the channels, seizes the neck and head and stirs up kapha, causing wheezing breathlessness; the patient finds relief sitting up and welcomes warmth. It worsens with clouds, cold and kapha-increasing things.

The patient with hikka-shvasa is first anointed with oil mixed with salt and given sudation; this loosens the adherent kapha in the channels, after which vamana or other purification is given according to strength.
Inability to speak in full sentences, bluish lips, SpO2 below 92%, silent chest or exhaustion need emergency referral. Rescue inhalers must not be stopped.

verses.topic: Prescribed diabetes medicines and danger signs
verses.meaning: Prescribed glucose-lowering medicines must not be stopped without the prescribing doctor; Ayurvedic treatment is added with sugar monitoring. Foot ulcers, drowsiness, or extreme thirst with weight loss need referral.

verses.topic: Poisonous drugs need shodhana and exact dose
verses.meaning: Visha and upavisha dravyas such as Vatsanabha, Kupilu and Bhallataka are used only after shodhana, in exact small doses, for a limited period, under supervision.
